nodes.name: Direct sum result
nodes.statement: A direct sum result for a relation $f$ in a model of communication  (roughly) states that in order to compute $k$ independent  instances of $f$ simultaneously, if we provide communication less than $k$ times the communication required to compute $f$ with the constant success probability $p<1$, then the success probability for computing all the $k$ instances of $f$ correctly is at most a constant $q<1$.
nodes.statement_short: A direct sum result: with less than k times the communication for one instance, success on all k instances is at most a constant q<1.

nodes.name: Direct product result
nodes.statement: A direct product result, which is a stronger result, states that in such a situation  the success probability for computing all the $k$ instances of $f$ correctly is at most $p^{-\Omega(k)}$.
nodes.statement_short: A direct product result: in the same situation, success on all k instances decays exponentially in k.

nodes.name: Task T1 (quantum state transfer with side state)
nodes.statement: \noindent {\bf T1}:  Alice gets to know the eigen-decomposition of a quantum state $\rho$. Alice and Bob get to know the eigen-decomposition of a quantum state $\sigma$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$. They also know $c \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, the relative entropy between $\rho$ and $\sigma$ and an error parameter ${\varepsilon}$. They  use shared entanglement and communication and at the end of the protocol, Bob ends up with a quantum state $\tilde{\rho}$ such that $\mathrm{F}(\rho, \tilde{\rho}) \geq 1 - {\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Alice knows rho, both know sigma and S(rho||sigma); with entanglement and communication Bob must output a state of fidelity at least 1-eps with rho.

nodes.name: Jain-Radhakrishnan-Sen compression to relative entropy
nodes.statement: Jain, Radhakrishnan and Sen in~\cite{Jain:2005:PEM:1068502.1068658,Jain:2008}, showed that this task  (for constant ${\varepsilon}$) can be achieved with  communication $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma} +1)$ bits, and this led to direct sum theorems for all relations in  entanglement-assisted quantum one-way and entanglement-assisted quantum simultaneous message-passing communication models.
assumptions: (for constant ${\varepsilon}$)
conclusions: this task  (for constant ${\varepsilon}$) can be achieved with  communication $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma} +1)$ bits
nodes.statement_short: Task T1 can be achieved with O(S(rho||sigma)+1) bits, giving direct sum theorems for entanglement-assisted one-way and SMP models.

nodes.name: Jain-Radhakrishnan-Sen classical sampling with public coins
nodes.statement: They also considered the special case when the inputs to Alice and Bob are probability distributions $P,Q$ respectively and showed that sharing public random coins and $\CMcal{O}(\relent{P}{Q}+1))$ bits of  communication can achieve this task (for constant ${\varepsilon}$).
assumptions: the inputs to Alice and Bob are probability distributions $P,Q$ respectively
conclusions: sharing public random coins and $\CMcal{O}(\relent{P}{Q}+1))$ bits of  communication can achieve this task

nodes.name: Harsha-Jain-McAllester-Radhakrishnan exact sampling
nodes.statement: Later an improved result was obtained by Harsha, Jain, Mc. Allester and Radhakrishnan~\cite{Harsha:2010}, where they presented a protocol in which Bob is able to sample exactly from $P$ with expected communication $\relent{P}{Q}+2\log\relent{P}{Q}+\CMcal{O}(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bob can sample exactly from P with expected communication S(P||Q)+2 log S(P||Q)+O(1).

nodes.name: [n]
nodes.statement: For integer $n \geq 1$, let $[n]$ represent the set $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$.

nodes.name: log and ln
nodes.statement: We let $\log$ represent logarithm to the base $2$ and $\ln$ represent logarithm to the base $\mathrm{e}$.

nodes.name: Cross product of sets
nodes.statement: Let $\finset{X}$ and $\finset{Y}$ be finite sets. $\finset{X}\times\finset{Y}$ represents the cross product of $\finset{X}$ and $\finset{Y}$.

nodes.name: Set power X^k
nodes.statement:
For a natural number $k$, we let 
$\finset{X}^k$ denote the set $\finset{X}\times\cdots\times\finset{X}$, the cross product of
$\finset{X}$, $k$ times.

nodes.name: Probability mu(x)
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on $\finset{X}$. We let $\mu(x)$ represent the probability of $x\in\finset{X}$ according to $\mu$.

nodes.name: Expectation value
l1 and l2 norms
nodes.statement: The $\ell_1$ norm of an operator $X$ on $\CMcal{H}$ is $\onenorm{X}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }\sqrt{X^{\dag}X}$ and $\ell_2$ norm is $\norm{X}_2\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } XX^{\dag}}$.

nodes.name: Quantum state
nodes.statement: A quantum state (or a density matrix or just a state) is a positive semi-definite matrix with trace equal to $1$.

nodes.name: Pure state
nodes.statement: It is called {\em pure} if and only if the rank is $1$.

nodes.name: Sub-normalized state
nodes.statement: A sub-normalized state is a positive semi-definite matrix with trace less than or equal to $1$.
differentia: with trace less than or equal to $1$

nodes.name: Pure state notation psi
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a unit vector on $\CMcal{H}$, that is $\langle \psi,\psi \rangle=1$.  With some abuse of notation, we use $\psi$ to represent the state and also the density matrix $\ketbra{\psi}$, associated with $\ket{\psi}$.

nodes.name: Computational basis
nodes.statement: Fix an orthonormal basis on $\CMcal{H}$, referred to as {\em computational basis}.

nodes.name: Complex conjugate of a vector
nodes.statement: Let $\conjugate{\ket{\psi}}$ represent the complex conjugation of $\ket{\psi}$, taken in the computational basis.

nodes.name: Support of a state
nodes.statement: Given a quantum state $\rho$ on $\CMcal{H}$, {\em support of $\rho$}, called $\text{supp}(\rho)$ is the subspace of $\CMcal{H}$ spanned by all eigen-vectors of $\rho$ with non-zero eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Quantum register
nodes.statement: A {\em quantum register} $A$ is associated with some Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A$.

nodes.name: Register dimension |A|
nodes.statement: Define $|A| \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \dim(\CMcal{H}_A)$.

nodes.name: Linear operators L(A)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}(A)$ represent the set of all linear operators on $\CMcal{H}_A$.

nodes.name: States D(A)
nodes.statement: We denote by $\mathcal{D}(A)$, the set of quantum states on the Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A$.

nodes.name: Subscript register notation
nodes.statement: State $\rho$ with subscript $A$ indicates $\rho_A \in \mathcal{D}(A)$.

nodes.name: Register equivalence
nodes.statement: If two registers $A,B$ are associated with the same Hilbert space, we shall represent the relation by $A\equiv B$.

nodes.name: Composition of registers
nodes.statement: Composition of two registers $A$ and $B$, denoted $AB$, is associated with Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B$.

nodes.name: Tensor product of states
nodes.statement: For two quantum states $\rho\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ and $\sigma\in \mathcal{D}(B)$, $\rho\otimes\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ represents the tensor product (Kronecker product) of $\rho$ and $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Identity operator I_A
nodes.statement: The identity operator on $\CMcal{H}_A$ (and associated register $A$) is denoted $I_A$.

nodes.name: Partial trace
nodes.statement:
Let $\rho_{AB} \in \mathcal{D}(AB)$. We define
\[ \rho_{\reg{B}} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \partrace{\reg{A}}{\rho_{AB}}
\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i (\bra{i} \otimes I_{\cspace{B}})
\rho_{AB} (\ket{i} \otimes I_{\cspace{B}}) , \]
where $\set{\ket{i}}_i$ is an orthonormal basis for the Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A$.
nodes.statement_short: Partial trace over A of a bipartite state, defined via an orthonormal basis of A.

nodes.name: Marginal state
nodes.statement: The state $\rho_B\in \mathcal{D}(B)$ is referred to as the marginal state of $\rho_{AB}$.

nodes.name: Missing-register convention
nodes.statement: Unless otherwise stated, a missing register from subscript in a state will represent partial trace over that register.

nodes.name: Purification
nodes.statement: Given a $\rho_A\in\mathcal{D}(A)$, a {\em purification} of $\rho_A$ is a pure state $\rho_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ such that $\partrace{\reg{B}}{\rho_{AB}}=\rho_A$.

nodes.name: Quantum map (CPTP)
nodes.statement: A quantum {map} $\mathcal{E}: \mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$ is a completely positive and trace preserving (CPTP) linear map (mapping states in $\mathcal{D}(A)$ to states in $\mathcal{D}(B)$).

nodes.name: Unitary operator
nodes.statement: A {\em unitary} operator $U_A:\CMcal{H}_A \rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A$ is such that $U_A^{\dagger}U_A = U_A U_A^{\dagger} = I_A$.

nodes.name: Isometry
nodes.statement: An {\em isometry}  $V:\CMcal{H}_A \rightarrow \CMcal{H}_B$ is such that $V^{\dagger}V = I_A$ and $VV^{\dagger} = I_B$.

nodes.name: Set of unitaries U(A)
nodes.statement: The set of all unitary operations on register $A$ is  denoted by $\mathcal{U}(A)$.

nodes.name: Information theoretic quantities (fidelity, entropy, relative entropy, relative max-entropy, mutual information, conditional mutual information)
nodes.statement: We shall consider the following information theoretic quantities. Let $A$ be a quantum register. Let $\varepsilon \geq 0$. \begin{enumerate} \item {\bf Fidelity} For $\rho,\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, $$\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\onenorm{\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}}.$$ For classical probability distributions $P = \{p_i\}, Q =\{q_i\}$, $$\mathrm{F}(P,Q)\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i \sqrt{p_i \cdot q_i}.$$ \item {\bf Entropy} For $\rho\in\mathcal{D}(A)$, $$S(\rho_A) \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } - \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\rho_A\log\rho_A) .$$ \item {\bf Relative entropy} For $\rho,\sigma\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$, $$\relent{\rho}{\sigma} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\rho\log\rho) - \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\rho\log\sigma) .$$ \item {\bf Relative max-entropy} For $\rho,\sigma\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$, $$ \rminent{\rho}{\sigma} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \inf \{ \lambda \in \mathbb{R} : 2^{\lambda} \sigma \geq \rho \} .$$ \item {\bf Mutual information} For $\rho_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$, $$\mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } S(\rho_A) + S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}) = \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\rho_A\otimes\rho_B}.$$ \item {\bf Conditional mutual information} For $\rho_{ABC}\in\mathcal{D}(ABC)$, $$\condmutinf{A}{B}{C}_{\rho}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \mutinf{A}{BC}_{\rho}-\mutinf{A}{C}_{\rho}.$$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Defines fidelity, von Neumann entropy, relative entropy, relative max-entropy, mutual information and conditional mutual information.
nodes.label: def:infquant

nodes.name: Fidelity vs trace distance (Fuchs-van de Graaf)
nodes.statement: For quantum states $\rho,\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, it holds that \[2(1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma))\leq\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}\leq2\sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)^2}.\] For two pure states $\ket{\phi}$ and $\ket{\psi}$, we have \[\onenorm{\phi-\psi}=2 \sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\phi, \psi)^2}=2 \sqrt{1-\abs{\langle\phi|\psi\rangle}^2}.\]
assumptions: For quantum states $\rho,\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$
nodes.statement_short: Trace distance is sandwiched between 2(1-F) and 2 sqrt(1-F^2), with equality on the right for pure states.
nodes.label: fact:tracefidelityequi

nodes.name: Stinespring representation
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Stinespring representation}) Let $\mathcal{E}(\cdot): \mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$ be a quantum operation. There exists a Hilbert space $C$ and an unitary $U: A \otimes B \otimes C \rightarrow A \otimes B\otimes C$ such that $\mathcal{E}(\omega)=\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A,C}\br{U (\omega \otimes \ketbra{0}^{B,C}) U^{\dagger}}$. Stinespring representation for a channel is not unique.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{E}(\cdot): \mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$ be a quantum operation.
conclusions: There exists a Hilbert space $C$ and an unitary
nodes.statement_short: Every quantum operation is a partial trace of a unitary acting on the input with ancillas.
nodes.label: stinespring

nodes.name: Monotonicity under quantum operations
nodes.statement: For states $\rho$, $\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, and quantum operation $\mathcal{E}(\cdot):\mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$, it holds that \begin{align*} \onenorm{\mathcal{E}(\rho) - \mathcal{E}(\sigma)} \leq \onenorm{\rho - \sigma} \quad \mbox{and} \quad \mathrm{F}(\mathcal{E}(\rho),\mathcal{E}(\sigma)) \geq \mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma) \quad \mbox{and} \quad \relent{\rho}{\sigma}\geq \relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}. \end{align*} In particular, for bipartite states $\rho^{AB},\sigma^{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$, it holds that \begin{align*} \onenorm{\rho^{AB} - \sigma^{AB}} \geq \onenorm{\rho^A - \sigma^A} \quad \mbox{and} \quad \mathrm{F}(\rho^{AB},\sigma^{AB}) \leq \mathrm{F}(\rho^A,\sigma^A) \quad \mbox{and} \quad \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}\geq \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} . \end{align*}
assumptions: For states $\rho$, $\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, and quantum operation $\mathcal{E}(\cdot):\mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$
nodes.statement_short: Trace distance and relative entropy do not increase, and fidelity does not decrease, under quantum operations (and partial trace).
nodes.label: fact:monotonequantumoperation

nodes.name: l1 distance vs l2 distance of square roots
nodes.statement: Let $A, B$ be two positive semidefinite operators on Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$. Then \[\onenorm{A-B}\geq\norm{\sqrt{A}-\sqrt{B}}^2_2.\]
assumptions: Let $A, B$ be two positive semidefinite operators on Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$.
nodes.label: fact:onenorm vs twonorm

nodes.name: Tr sqrt(rho) sqrt(sigma) lower bound
nodes.statement: Given two quantum states $\rho$ and $\sigma$, $$\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}\geq 1 - \frac{1}{2} \onenorm{ \rho - \sigma} \geq 1-\sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)^2} .$$
assumptions: Given two quantum states $\rho$ and $\sigma$
nodes.label: fact:fidelityvstrace

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 2.6
nodes.statement: By Facts~\ref{fact:onenorm vs twonorm} and~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi}, \[2\sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)^2}\geq \onenorm{ \rho - \sigma } \geq\norm{\sqrt{\rho}-\sqrt{\sigma}}_2^2=2-2 \cdot \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }\br{\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}}. \tag*{\qedhere}\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine Fact 2.5 (l1 vs l2) with Fact 2.2 (fidelity vs trace distance).

nodes.name: Joint concavity of fidelity
nodes.statement: [\cite{Watrouslecturenote}, Proposition 4.7] Given states $\rho_1,\rho_2\ldots\rho_k,\sigma_1,\sigma_2\ldots\sigma_k$ and positive numbers $p_1,p_2\ldots p_k$ such that $\sum_ip_i=1$. Then $$\mathrm{F}(\sum_ip_i\rho_i,\sum_ip_i\sigma_i)\geq \sum_ip_i\mathrm{F}(\rho_i,\sigma_i).$$
assumptions: Given states $\rho_1,\rho_2\ldots\rho_k,\sigma_1,\sigma_2\ldots\sigma_k$ and positive numbers $p_1,p_2\ldots p_k$ such that $\sum_ip_i=1$.
nodes.label: fact:fidconcave

nodes.name: Quantum substate theorem
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Quantum substrate theorem}) Given $\rho, \sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$. For any ${\varepsilon}>0$, there exists $\rho'\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ such that \[\mathrm{F}(\rho,\rho')\geq1-{\varepsilon}\quad \mbox{and}\quad \rminent{\rho'}{\sigma}\leq\frac{\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1}{{\varepsilon}}+\log\frac{1}{1-{\varepsilon}}.\]
assumptions: Given $\rho, \sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$.
For any ${\varepsilon}>0$
nodes.statement_short: A state close in fidelity to rho has relative max-entropy w.r.t. sigma bounded by (S(rho||sigma)+1)/eps + log 1/(1-eps).
nodes.label: fact:substrate

nodes.name: Gentle measurement lemma
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Gentle measurement lemma}) Let $\rho\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ and $\Pi$ be a projector. Then, \[\mathrm{F}(\rho,\frac{\Pi \rho \Pi}{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \Pi \rho })\geq \sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \Pi \rho}.\]
assumptions: Let $\rho\in \mathcal{D}(A)$  and $\Pi$ be a projector.
nodes.label: fact:gentlemeasurement

nodes.name: Proof of the gentle measurement lemma
nodes.statement: Introduce a register $B$, such that $|B|\geq |A|$. Let $\phi\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ be a purification of $\rho$. Then $( \Pi \otimes I_B)\phi ( \Pi \otimes I_B)$ is a purification of $\Pi \rho \Pi $. Hence (using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation, Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}) \[\mathrm{F}(\rho, \frac{\Pi \rho \Pi}{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \Pi \rho } )\mathrm{F}\br{\phi,(\Pi\otimes I_B)\phi(\Pi\otimes I_B)}= \frac{\abs{\bra{\phi}(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}}{\norm{(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}} = \sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }( \Pi \rho)}. \tag*{\qedhere} \]
nodes.statement_short: Purify rho, note the projected purification purifies the post-measurement state, and use monotonicity of fidelity.

nodes.name: Trace of exp(log sigma_AB - log sigma_A + log rho_A) is less than 1
nodes.statement: Given quantum states $\sigma_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB), \rho_A\in \mathcal{D}(A)$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho_A)\subset\text{supp}(\sigma_A)$, it holds that $$\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)})<1.$$
assumptions: Given quantum states $\sigma_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB), \rho_A\in \mathcal{D}(A)$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho_A)\subset\text{supp}(\sigma_A)$
nodes.label: fact:ruskai

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 2.11
nodes.statement: Consider, \begin{eqnarray*} \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}) &<& \int_{0}^{\infty}du\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sigma_{AB}\frac{1}{\sigma_A+uI_A}\rho_A\frac{1}{\sigma_A+uI_A}) \quad (\text{Theorem} 5, ~\cite{ruskai2002} ) \\ &=& \int_{0}^{\infty}du\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\frac{1}{\sigma_A+uI_A}\sigma_{A}\frac{1}{\sigma_A+uI_A}\rho_A) \\ &=& \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sigma_{A}\int_{0}^{\infty}du\frac{1}{(\sigma_A+uI_A)^2}\rho_A) = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sigma_A\sigma^{-1}_A\rho_A) =1. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lieb-Ruskai's integral bound (Theorem 5 of Ruskai 2002) and evaluate the integral.

nodes.name: Strong subadditivity theorem
nodes.statement: ~\cite{Lieb:1973,LiebR:1973}(\textbf{Strong subadditivity theorem}) For any tripartite quantum state $\rho\in\mathcal{D}(ABC)$, it holds that $\condmutinf{A}{C}{B}_{\rho}\geq0$.
assumptions: For any tripartite quantum state $\rho\in\mathcal{D}(ABC)$
nodes.label: fact:strongsubadditivity

nodes.name: Araki-Lieb inequality and subadditivity
nodes.statement: For a quantum state $\rho_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$, it holds that $\abs{\mathrm{S}(\rho_A)-\mathrm{S}(\rho_B)}\leq\mathrm{S}(\rho_{AB})\leq\mathrm{S}(\rho_A)+\mathrm{S}(\rho_B)$. Furthermore, \[\mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho}=\mathrm{S}(\rho_A)+\mathrm{S}(\rho_B)-\mathrm{S}(\rho_{AB})\leq 2\mathrm{S}(\rho_A).\]
assumptions: For a quantum state $\rho_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$
nodes.label: fact:conditionalmutinf

nodes.name: Chain rule lower bound for conditional mutual information with independent registers
nodes.statement: Let $\rho_{A_1A_2\ldots A_kBC} \in \mathcal{D}(A_1\cdots A_k BC)$ such that $\rho_{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}=\rho_{A_1}\otimes\rho_{A_2}\otimes\ldots\rho_{A_k}$. Then, \[\condmutinf{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}{B}{C}_{\rho}\geq\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{A_i}{B}{C}_{\rho}.\]
assumptions: such that $\rho_{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}=\rho_{A_1}\otimes\rho_{A_2}\otimes\ldots\rho_{A_k}$
nodes.label: fact:chainrulemutualinf

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 2.13
nodes.statement: Consider, \begin{eqnarray*} \condmutinf{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}{B}{C}_{\rho}&=&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{B}{A_1C}_\rho\\ &=&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\mutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{A_1BC}_{\rho}-\mutinf{A_1}{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}\rho\\ &=&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\mutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{A_1BC}_{\rho}\\ &\geq&\condmutinf{A_1}{B}{C}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{A_2A_3\ldots A_k}{B}{C}_{\rho} \end{eqnarray*} The first and second equalities follow from the definition of the conditional mutual information. The third equality is from the independence between $A_1$ and $A_2A_3\ldots A_k$. The last inequality is from strong subadditivity (Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}). Proof follows by induction.
nodes.statement_short: By induction on k: chain rule, independence of A_1, and strong subadditivity.

nodes.name: Relative entropy chain rule for classical-quantum states
nodes.statement: Given $\rho_{AB},\sigma_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$, such that $\text{supp}(\sigma_{AB})\subset \text{supp}(\rho_{AB})$, $\rho_{AB} = \sum_a \mu(a) \ketbra{a}_A \otimes\rho^a_B$ and $\sigma_{AB} = \sum_a \mu'(a) \ketbra{a}_A \otimes\sigma^a_B$, where $\rho^a_B,\sigma^a_B\in \mathcal{D}(B)$, $\mu(a),\mu'(a)\geq 0$ and $\sum_a\mu(a)=1,\sum_a\mu'(a)=1$. It holds from the definition of relative entropy that \[ \relent{\sigma_{AB}}{\rho_{AB}} = \relent{\mu}{\mu'} + \expec{a\leftarrow \mu'} {\relent{\sigma^a_B}{\rho^a_B}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Relative entropy of two cq-states splits into the classical relative entropy plus the averaged conditional relative entropy.
nodes.label: fact:relative entropy splitting

nodes.name: Mutual information of a classical-quantum state (Holevo quantity)
nodes.statement: Given a classical-quantum state $\rho_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ of the form $\rho_{AB} = \sum_a \mu(a) \ketbra{a}_A \otimes \rho^a_B$, where $\rho^a_B\in\mathcal{D}(B)$ and $\sum_a \mu(a)=1$, $\mu(a)\geq 0$, we have \[ \mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho} = \mathrm{S}\br{\sum_a\mu(a)\rho_a}-\sum_a\mu(a)\mathrm{S}\br{\rho_a},\]

nodes.name: Conditional mutual information of a state classical on C
nodes.statement: Let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a state of the form $\rho_{ABC}=\sum_c \mu(c)\ketbra{c}_{C}\otimes \rho^c_{AB}$, where $\rho^c_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$ and $\sum_c\mu(c)=1$, $\mu(c)\geq 0$. Then $$\condmutinf{A}{B}{C}_{\rho}=\sum_c \mu(c)\mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho^c}.$$
assumptions: Let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a state of the form $\rho_{ABC}=\sum_c \mu(c)\ketbra{c}_{C}\otimes \rho^c_{AB}$, where $\rho^c_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$ and $\sum_c\mu(c)=1$, $\mu(c)\geq 0$.
nodes.label: fact:cqcondmut

nodes.name: Entanglement assisted quantum one-way communication protocol
nodes.statement: Let $f\subseteq\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}\times\CMcal{Z}$ be a relation. Alice holds input $x \in \CMcal{X}$ and Bob holds input $y \in \CMcal{Y}$. They may share prior quantum states independent of the inputs. Alice makes a unitary transformation on her qubits, based on her input $x$, and sends part of her qubits to Bob. Bob makes a unitary operation, based on his input $y$, and measures the last few qubits (answer registers) in the computational basis to get the answer $z \in \CMcal{Z}$. The answer is declared correct if $(x,y,z)\in f$.
nodes.statement_short: One-way model: Alice applies an input-dependent unitary, sends qubits; Bob applies a unitary and measures; correct if (x,y,z) is in f.

nodes.name: Quantum one-way communication complexity Q^{ent,A->B}_eps(f)
nodes.statement: Let $\qcc{{\varepsilon}}{f}$ represent the quantum one-way communication complexity of $f$ with worst case error ${\varepsilon}$, that is minimum number of qubits Alice needs to send to Bob, over all protocols computing $f$ with error at most ${\varepsilon}$ on \textit{any} input $(x,y)$.

nodes.name: Distributional quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement: We let $\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}}{f}$ represent distributional quantum one-way communication complexity of $f$ under distribution $\mu$ over $\CMcal{X}\times \CMcal{Y}$ with distributional error at most ${\varepsilon}$. This is the communication cost of the best protocol computing $f$ with maximum error ${\varepsilon}$ averaged over distribution $\mu$.

nodes.name: Quantum compression protocol P (relative entropy compression)
nodes.statement: Given quantum states $\rho,\sigma$ on a Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$ with dimension $N$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$. Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ and Bob is given the eigen-decomposition of $\sigma$. Let $\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$ and ${\varepsilon} >0$ be known to Alice and Bob. There exists an entanglement assisted quantum one-way communication protocol, with Alice sending $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}$ that Bob outputs at the end of the protocol satisfies $\mathrm{F}(\rho,\tilde{\rho})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$ .
also_stated_at: \noindent $\mathcal{P}$: Let $\rho,\sigma$ be quantum states such that $\relent{\rho}{\sigma} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (\rho \log \rho - \rho \log \sigma)$, the relative entropy between $\rho$ and $\sigma$, is finite. Alice gets to know the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$. Bob gets to know the eigen-decomposition of $\sigma$. Both Alice and Bob know $ \relent{\rho}{\sigma}$ and an error parameter ${\varepsilon}$. Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and after communication of $\CMcal{O}((\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits from Alice to Bob, Bob ends up with a quantum state $\tilde{\rho}$ such that $\mathrm{F}(\rho, \tilde{\rho}) \geq 1 - 5{\varepsilon}$, where $\mathrm{F}(\cdot)$ represents fidelity.

Bob gets to know the eigen-decomposition of a quantum state $\sigma\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$. Both Alice and Bob know $ \relent{\rho}{\sigma} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \rho \log \rho - \rho \log \sigma$, the relative entropy between $\rho$ and $\sigma$ and an error parameter ${\varepsilon}$. Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and after communication of $\CMcal{O}((\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits from Alice to Bob, Bob ends up with a quantum state $\tilde{\rho}$ such that $\mathrm{F}(\rho, \tilde{\rho}) \geq 1 - {\varepsilon}$, where $\mathrm{F}(\cdot,\cdot)$ represents {\em fidelity}.

nodes.name: Quantum compression protocol P
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Input:} Alice is given $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$. Bob is given $\sigma=\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$.
\bigskip



\textbf{Shared resources:} Alice and Bob hold $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$ registers $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ ($i \in [\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil]$), such that $A_1^i\equiv A_1, A^i_2\equiv A_2, B_1^i\equiv B_1,B_2^i\equiv B_2$. The shared state in register $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ is $\ket{S}_{A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i}$. Let $i$ refer to the `index' of corresponding registers.

They also share infinitely many random hash functions $h_1,h_2,\cdots$, where each $h_l:\set{0,\cdots,N-1}\rightarrow\set{0,1}$.

\begin{enumerate}

\item \textbf{For} $i=1$ to $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$,

\begin{enumerate}

\item Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I_A- P_A}$ on each register $A_1^iA^i_2$ where,
\begin{equation} P_A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) .
\end{equation}

On each index $i$, she declares \textit{success} if her outcome corresponds to $P_A$.

\item Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I_B- P_B}$ on each register $B_1^iB^i_2$ where,
\begin{equation} P_B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'} b_i,K\}}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) .
\end{equation}

On each index $i$, he declares \textit{success} if his outcome corresponds to $P_B$.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Endfor}

\item If Alice does not succeed on any index, she aborts.

\item Else, Alice selects the first index $m$ where she succeeds and sends to Bob the binary encoding of $k=\lceil m/N\rceil$ using $\lceil\log\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil$ bits.  

\item Alice sends $\{ h_l(m\mod N) |~ l \in  [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]\}$  to Bob.

\item  Define $S_B \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \{ t |~ \text{ Bob succeeds on index } $t$\} \cap \{(k-1)N,  \cdots, k N -1\}$. If $S_B$ is empty, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$. Bob selects the first index $n$ in $S_B$ such that $\forall l \in  [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]: h_l(n \mod N) = h_l(m \mod N) $ and outputs the state in $B_1^n$ (if no such index exists, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$).
nodes.statement_short: Alice and Bob measure shared entangled copies with acceptance projectors; Alice sends the block of her first success and hash values; Bob outputs the matching accepted copy.

nodes.name: Overlap bound for eigenvectors of rho' with small sigma-eigenvalues
nodes.statement: Let $\rho'$ have the eigen-decomposition $\rho' = \sum_i g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i}$. For any $p>0$ and every $\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i}$, we have $\sum_{j|~b_j\leq p\cdot g_i}\abs{\braket{b_j}{g_i}}^2 \leq 2^{c'}\cdot p$.

For any $p>0$ and every $\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i}$

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.3
nodes.statement: Since $\rho' \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$, it implies $g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i} \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$. Let $\Pi$ be the projection onto the eigen-space of $\sigma$ with eigenvalues less than or equal to $p\cdot g_i$. We have $\Pi\sigma\Pi \leq p\cdot g_i\cdot\Pi$. After applying $\Pi$ on both sides of the equation $g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i} \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$ and taking operator norm on both sides, we get $g_i\sum_{j:~b_j \leq p\cdot g_i}\abs{\braket{b_j}{g_i}}^2 \leq 2^{c'}\cdot p \cdot g_i $. This implies the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Project the operator inequality g_i|g_i><g_i| <= 2^{c'} sigma onto the small-eigenvalue eigenspace of sigma and take norms.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.5
nodes.statement: Consider, \begin{equation*} (I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_{i,j=1}^N\ket{\conjugate{g_j}} \ket{b_i}\braket{b_i}{g_j} \left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\lceil Kg_j\rceil, \frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'}b_i\}}\ket{m, m} \right). \end{equation*} Therefore, \begin{align} & \norm{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')} }^2 \geq \sum_{i,j=1}^N \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \min\{g_j, \frac{1}{\delta}2^{c'}b_i \} \nonumber \\ & \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j \left(\sum_{i|~b_i\geq \delta 2^{-c'}g_j} \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \right) \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j(1- \delta) = 1- \delta . \quad \mbox{(using Claim~\ref{claim:1})} \end{align} Using the above, \begin{align*} & \prob{\text{Bob succeeds}|~\text{Alice succeeds}} = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)} \\ & \geq \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho')} - \frac{1}{2} \onenorm{S_A(\rho) - S_A(\rho')} \\ & = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho')} - \sqrt{1- \abs{\braket{S_A(\rho)}{S_A(\rho')}}^2} \quad \mbox{(Fact~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi})} \\ & \geq 1 - \delta - 2 \sqrt{ (1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\rho'))^{1/2}} . \quad \mbox{(Claim~\ref{claim:2} and Eq.~\eqref{eq:probonrho'})} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound Bob's acceptance on S_A(rho') via Claim 3.3, then transfer to S_A(rho) using Claim 3.4 and trace distance.

nodes.name: Bob's acceptance on S_A(rho')
nodes.statement: & \norm{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')} }^2 \geq \sum_{i,j=1}^N \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \min\{g_j, \frac{1}{\delta}2^{c'}b_i \} \nonumber \\ & \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j \left(\sum_{i|~b_i\geq \delta 2^{-c'}g_j} \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \right) \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j(1- \delta) = 1- \delta . \quad \mbox{(using Claim~\ref{claim:1})}

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.6
nodes.statement: From gentle measurement lemma (Fact~\ref{fact:gentlemeasurement}), $$\mathrm{F}(S_A(\rho), \frac{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)} (I_A\otimes P_B) }{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)}}) \geq \sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)}}. $$ Since the marginal of $\ket{S_A(\rho)}$ on register $B$ is $\rho$ and partial trace does not decrease fidelity (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}), using item 2. above, the desired result follows.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.11
nodes.statement: Following equality follows from definitions. \begin{equation*} \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} = \relent{\rho_{AB}}{e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}} \enspace . \end{equation*} Define, $$Z= \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}) \quad ; \quad \tau_{AB}=e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}/Z \enspace .$$ It holds that $Z\leq 1$ (from Fact \ref{fact:ruskai}) and hence $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}} \leq \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$. Bob computes the eigen-decomposition of $\tau_{AB}$ using his input. They run the protocol given by Theorem~\ref{thm:protocol} with the following setting: Alice knows a state $\rho_{AB}$, Bob knows a state $\tau_{AB}$ and both know a number ($=\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$) greater than $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}}$. They also know the error parameter ${\varepsilon}>0$. By the virtue of Remark \ref{qbevremark}, at the end of the protocol, Bob obtains a state $\tilde{\rho}_{AB}$, such that $\mathrm{F}(\rho_{AB},\tilde{\rho}_{AB})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$. Communication from Alice is upper bounded by $\CMcal{O}(\br{\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} +1}/\epsilon^4)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.12
nodes.statement: Let a Stinespring representation of $\mathcal{E}$ be $\mathcal{E}(\omega) = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A,C}\br{V (\omega \ketbra{0}_{BC})V^{\dagger}}$, where $V:\CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B \otimes \CMcal{H}_C \rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B\otimes \CMcal{H}_C$ is a unitary operation (Fact~\ref{stinespring}). Alice and Bob compute the states $V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ and $V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ , respectively. From Lemma~\ref{lem:withsideinf} and the equality $\relent{V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}}V^{\dagger}}{V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}}=\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, there exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4 $ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}$ that Bob gets at the end of the protocol satisfies $\mathrm{F}(V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger},\tilde{\rho}_{ABC})\geq1-5{\varepsilon}$. Bob outputs $\tilde{\rho} = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{BC} V^{\dagger}\br{\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}} V $. From monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}), $\mathrm{F}(\rho, \tilde{\rho} )\geq1-5{\varepsilon}$.

nodes.name: Direct sum theorem for entanglement-assisted quantum one-way communication
nodes.statement: Let $\CMcal{X},\CMcal{Y},\CMcal{Z}$ be finite sets, $f\subseteq\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}\times\CMcal{Z}$ be a relation, $0<{\varepsilon},\delta$ be error parameters and $k>1$ be an integer. We have \[\dqcc{}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq \Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
assumptions: Let $\CMcal{X},\CMcal{Y},\CMcal{Z}$ be finite sets, $f\subseteq\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}\times\CMcal{Z}$ be a relation, $0<{\varepsilon},\delta$ be error parameters and $k>1$ be an integer.
nodes.statement_short: Computing k copies of f one-way with entanglement needs about k times delta^9 times the cost of one copy.
nodes.label: thm:directsumoneway

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be any distribution over $\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}$. We show the following, which combined with Fact~\ref{fact:yaos principle} implies the desired: \[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\] Let $\CMcal{Q}$ be a quantum one-way protocol with communication $c\cdot k$ computing $f^k$ with overall probability of success at least $1-{\varepsilon}$ under distribution $\mu^k$. Let the inputs to Alice and Bob be given in registers $X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. For brevity, we define $X\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. Thus, the state $\sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}$ represents the joint input, where $x$ is drawn from $X$ and $y$ is drawn from $Y$. Let $\sigma_{E_A,E_B}$ be the shared entanglement between Alice and Bob where register $E_A$ is with Alice and $E_B$ with Bob. Alice applies unitary $U:\CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$, where $E_A\equiv AM$, sends the message register $M$ to Bob, and then Bob applies the unitary $V: \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$, where $ME_B\equiv B'Z$. Since unitary operations by Alice and Bob are conditioned on their respective inputs, the unitaries $U,V$ are of the form $U=\sum_x\ketbra{x}_X\otimes U_x$ and $V=\sum_y\ketbra{y}_Y\otimes V_y$, where $U_x:\CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$ and $V_y: \CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$. Let the following be the global state before Alice applies her unitary: $$\theta_{XYE_AE_B} = \sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}\otimes\sigma_{E_AE_B}.$$ Let $D=D_1\cdots D_k$ be a random variable uniformly distributed over $\set{0,1}^k$ and independent of the input $XY$. Define random variables $U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$ such that $U_i=X_i$ if $D_i=0$ and $U_i=Y_i$ if $D_i=1$. Let $U=U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$. Consider the state $\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU}$, with registers $D,U$ as defined above. Let $\rho_{XYAME_BDU}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } U\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU} U^{\dagger}$ be the state after Alice applies her unitary and sends $M$ to Bob. Since $$\condmutinf{XE_AE_B}{Y}{DU}_{\theta}=0,$$ it holds that \[\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y}{DU}_{\rho}=0.\] From the definition of $DU$, we thus have (below $-i$ represents the set $\{1,2\ldots i-1,i+1\ldots k\}$), \begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_{-i}AE_BM}{Y}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y_{-i}}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=0. \end{equation} Since $\log\abs{M}\leq ck$ and register $E_B$ is independent of registers $XYDU$ in the state $\rho_{E_BXYDU}$, we have \begin{eqnarray*} \mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}&=&\mutinf{XYDU}{E_B}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{XYDU}{M}{E_B}_{\rho}\\ &=& \condmutinf{XYDU}{M}{E_B}_{\rho} \leq 2 \log\abs{M} \leq 2ck, \end{eqnarray*} where the second last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:conditionalmutinf}. Consider \begin{eqnarray*} 2ck&\geq& \mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}\geq \condmutinf{XY}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho}\\ &\geq&\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho} \quad (\text{Fact} ~\ref{fact:chainrulemutualinf})\\ &=& \sum_{i=1}^k \condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{D_iU_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho} \\ &=&\frac{1}{2}\br{\sum_{i=1}^k\br{\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{Y_i}{ME_B}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}}}\\ &\geq&\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}. \end{eqnarray*} where the last equality is from the definition of $DU$ and the last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}. Hence there exists $j\in[k]$ such that \begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_j}{ME_B}{Y_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}\leq 4c. \end{equation} Furthermore, we have \begin{equation} \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}= \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\theta} = 0. \end{equation} since the unitary by Alice does not change the state on registers $DUXY$. For brevity, set $B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } ME_B$. Define the following states, which are obtained by conditioning on various classical registers: $$\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}},$$ $$\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$ $$\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BYDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{YDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$ From~(\ref{eqn:dumarkov}), we have \[\condmutinf{Y}{B}{X_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}=0.\] which is equivalent to, using Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut} and the fact that registers $X,Y,U,D$ are classical in $\rho_B$: $$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}=0.$$ This implies $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ for all $x_j,y_j,d_{-j}u_{-j}$. From~(\ref{eqn:directsummessagelength}), and Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut}, $$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}\leq 4c.$$ Let $$G\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\set{(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j}):\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}\leq \frac{4c}{\delta}}.$$ By Markov's inequality, $$\prob{X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}\in G}\geq1-\delta. $$ Now, we exhibit an entanglement-assisted one-way protocol $\CMcal{Q}'$ for $f$ with communication less than $c$ and distributional error ${\varepsilon}$ under distribution $\mu$. \begin{mdframed} \bigskip \begin{enumerate} \item Alice and Bob share public coins according to distribution $\rho_{D_{-j}U_{-j}}$, and the shared entanglement needed to run the protocol $\CMcal{P}$ from Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol}. \item Alice and Bob are given the input $(x,y)\sim\mu$. They embed the input to the $j$-th coordinate $X_jY_j$. The input is independent of shared randomness, from equation (\ref{eqn:directsumpubliccoins}). \item Given input $(x_j,y_j)\equiv (x,y)$ and shared public coins $d_{-j}u_{-j}$, Alice knows the eigen-decomposition of the state $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, since $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$. Bob knows the eigen-decomposition of state $\rho_{B}^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$. \item They run the protocol in Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol} with inputs $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Alice) and $\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Bob). After communicating $\mathcal{O}(4c/\delta^9)$ bits to Bob, Bob receives a state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfying $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ if $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\in G$. \item Bob samples the distribution from $\rho_{Y_{-j}}$, since he has the registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. This is possible from equation \ref{eqn:dumarkov}, which states that register $Y_{-j}$ is independent of registers $A,B,X$ conditioned on registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. \item Bob applies the unitary $V$, as in the protocol $\CMcal{Q}$, on registers $BY\equiv E_BMY$ and then measures the register $Z$. He outputs the outcome. \end{enumerate} \end{mdframed} \bigskip From the protocol, it is clear that overall distributional error in $\CMcal{Q}'$ is at most $2\delta+{\varepsilon}$. The error $2\delta$ occurs since the state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfies $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ and the probability that $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\notin G$ is at most $\delta$. The error ${\varepsilon}$ is due to the original protocol $\CMcal{Q}$. Hence \[\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+2\delta}{f}\leq \CMcal{O}((c+1)/\delta^9),\] which implies (changing $\delta\rightarrow \frac{\delta}{2}$) \[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]

nodes.name: Quantum correlated sampling
nodes.statement: Let $\rho,\sigma$ be quantum states on a Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$ of dimension $N$. Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ and Bob is given the eigen-decomposition of $\sigma$. There exists a zero-communication protocol satisfying the following. \begin{enumerate} \item Alice outputs registers $A_1,A_2$ and and Bob outputs registers $B_1,B_2$ respectively, such that state in $A_1$ is $\rho$, the state in $B_1$ is $\sigma$ and $A_1\equiv B_1, A_2\equiv B_2$. \item Let $M = \{M_1,M_2\ldots M_w\}$ be a projective measurement, in the support of $A_1A_2$. Let $M$ be performed by Alice on the joint system $A_1A_2$ with outcome $I \in [w]$ and by Bob on the joint system $B_1B_2$ with outcome $J \in [w]$. Then $\Pr[I = J] \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^{3}$. \end{enumerate}
also_stated_at:
\noindent $\mathcal{P}_1:$ Given a register $A_1$, Alice gets to know the eigen-decomposition of a quantum state $\rho\in \mathcal{D}(A_1)$. Bob gets to know the eigen-decomposition of a quantum state $\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A_1)$. Alice and Bob use shared entanglement, do local measurements (no communication) and at the end Alice outputs registers $A_1A_2$ and Bob outputs registers $B_1B_2$ such that the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B_1\equiv A_1$ and $B_2\equiv A_2$.
\item The marginal state in register $A_1$ is $\rho$ and the marginal state in register $B_1$  is $\sigma$.
\item For any projective measurement $M  = \{M_1, \ldots , M_w\}$ such that $M_i \in \mathcal{L}(A_1A_2)$, the following holds. Let Alice perform $M$ on $A_1A_2$ and Bob perform $M$ on $B_1B_2$  and obtain outcomes $I \in [w], J \in [w]$ respectively. Then,
$$ \Pr[I = J]  \geq  \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^{3} . $$
\end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $\rho,\sigma$ be quantum states on a Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$ of dimension $N$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: Let eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$ and of $\sigma$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. Let $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{N}}$ be an orthonormal basis for $\CMcal{H}$. We assume that $a_1, \ldots, a_N, b_1, \ldots b_N$ are rational numbers and let $K$ be the least common multiple of their denominators. The error due to this assumption goes to $0$ as $K \rightarrow \infty$. Introduce registers $A_1,B_1$ associated to $\CMcal{H}$ and registers $A_2,B_2$ associated to some Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}'$ with an orthonormal basis $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{K}}$. Consider the following state shared in $A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2$. \begin{equation*} \ket{S}_{A_1B_1A_2B_2} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i=1}^N \ket{i,i}_{A_1B_1} \otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{K}\ket{m, m}_{A_2B_2} \right) \end{equation*} For brevity, define the registers $A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } A_1A_2$ and $B \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } B_1B_2$. The protocol is described below. \begin{mdframed} \bigskip \textbf{Input:} Alice is given $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$. Bob is given $\sigma=\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. \bigskip \textbf{Shared resources:} Alice and Bob hold infinitely many registers $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ ($i>0$), such that $A_1^i\equiv A_1, A^i_2\equiv A_2, B_1^i\equiv B_1,B_2^i\equiv B_2$. The shared state in register $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ is $\ket{S}_{A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i}$. Let $A \equiv A_1A_2$ and $B\equiv B_1B_2$ be used as output registers. Let $i$ refer to the `index' of corresponding registers. \begin{enumerate} \item For each $i>0$, Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I- P_A}$ on the registers $A^i_1A^i_2$, where \begin{equation*} P_A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) \end{equation*} She declares \textit{success} if she obtains outcome corresponding to $P_A$. She stops once she succeeds in some register $A^j$, and swaps $A^j$ with $A$. \item For each $i>0$, Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I- P_B}$ on the registers $B^i_1B^i_2$, where \begin{equation*} P_B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Kb_i}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) \end{equation*} He declares \textit{success} if he obtains outcome corresponding to $P_B$. He stops once he succeeds in some register $B^j$, and swaps $B^j$ with $B$. \end{enumerate} \end{mdframed} \bigskip At the end of above protocol, let the joint state in the register $AB$ be $\tau$. The following claim shows the first part of the theorem. \begin{claim} $\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A_2B_1B_2}(\tau)=\rho$ and $\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A_1A_2B_2}(\tau)=\sigma$. \end{claim} \begin{proof} It is easily seen that the marginal of the state $(P_A \otimes I_B) \ket{S}$ in register $A$ is $\rho$. Similarly the marginal of the state $(I_A \otimes P_B) \ket{S}$ in register $B$ in is $\sigma$. \end{proof} Following series of claims establish second part of the theorem. \begin{claim} \begin{equation*} \tau \geq \frac{(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}\bra{S}(P_A\otimes P_B) }{1 - \bra{S} (I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}} \enspace . \end{equation*} \end{claim} \begin{proof} Consider the event that Alice and Bob succeed at the same index. The resulting state in $AA_1BB_1$ is $$\frac{(P_A\otimes P_B ) \ket{S}\bra{S} (P_A\otimes P_B)}{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}},$$ and this event occurs with probability $$\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}^{i} \cdot \bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}= \frac{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}}{1 - \bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}}.$$ Since the cases of Bob succeeding before Alice and Alice succeeding before Bob add positive operators to $\tau$, we get the desired. \end{proof} \begin{claim} Let $\ket{\theta} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}{\norm{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}}$. Then $$\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^2}{1 + \sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}} \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^3 .$$ \end{claim} \begin{proof} Consider, \begin{align*} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} &\geq \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{1 - \bra{S} (I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}} & \mbox{(Claim~\ref{claim:tau})}\\ & = \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{2/N-\bra{S}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}} & \mbox{(using $\bra{S}P_A\otimes I_B\ket{S}=\bra{S}I_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}=1/N$)}. \end{align*} By direct calculation, we get $$(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i,j}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\braket{b_j}{a_i}\ket{b_j}\sum_{m=1}^{K\min(a_i,b_j)}\ket{m,m} ;$$ $$\ket{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_i\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\ket{a_i}\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m,m} .$$ Hence, \begin{equation} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2\right)^2}{2-\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2} . \end{equation} Define $R_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } a_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$ and $R'_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } b_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$. Note that both $\{R_{ij}\}$ and $\{R'_{ij}\}$ form probability distributions over $[N^2]$. Also note that $\mathrm{F}(R,R') = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})$. Consider (using relation between fidelity and $\ell_1$ distance, Facts~\ref{fact:fidelityvstrace} and~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi}), \begin{align} \sum_{i,j}\min(R_{ij},R'_{i,j}) & = 1 - \frac{1}{2}\onenorm{R-R'} \geq 1 - \sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(R,R')^2} \nonumber \\ &= 1 - \sqrt{1-(\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})^2} \geq 1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2} . \end{align} Combining Equations~\eqref{eq:thetatau} and~\eqref{eq:minR} we get the desired. \end{proof} \begin{claim} Let $M=\{M_1,M_2\ldots M_w\}$ be a projective measurement in the support of $A_1A_2$. Let $E=\sum_{i=1}^w M_i\otimes M_i$. Then $\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (E \ketbra{\theta}) = 1$. \end{claim} \begin{proof} Since $M_i$ is a projector in the support of $A_1A_2$, we have $(M_i\otimes M_i)\ket{\theta} = (M_i\otimes I)\ket{\theta}$. Hence, \[\bra{\theta}E\ket{\theta}=\sum_i\bra{\theta}M_i\otimes M_i\ket{\theta} = \sum_i\bra{\theta}M_i\otimes I\ket{\theta} = 1 . \tag*{\qedhere} \] \end{proof} Finally using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}) and Claim~\ref{overlaptau} we get the second part of the theorem as follows. \[\sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (E\tau)} \geq \mathrm{F}(\tau , \ketbra{\theta}) = \sqrt{\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta}} \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^{3/2} . \tag*{\qedhere} \]

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5.2
nodes.statement: It is easily seen that the marginal of the state $(P_A \otimes I_B) \ket{S}$ in register $A$ is $\rho$. Similarly the marginal of the state $(I_A \otimes P_B) \ket{S}$ in register $B$ in is $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Operator lower bound on the output state tau
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \tau \geq \frac{(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}\bra{S}(P_A\otimes P_B) }{1 - \bra{S} (I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}} \enspace . \end{equation*}
nodes.label: claim:tau

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5.3
nodes.statement: Consider the event that Alice and Bob succeed at the same index. The resulting state in $AA_1BB_1$ is $$\frac{(P_A\otimes P_B ) \ket{S}\bra{S} (P_A\otimes P_B)}{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}},$$ and this event occurs with probability $$\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}^{i} \cdot \bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}= \frac{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}}{1 - \bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}}.$$ Since the cases of Bob succeeding before Alice and Alice succeeding before Bob add positive operators to $\tau$, we get the desired.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the geometric series for the event that both succeed at the same index; other orders add positive operators.

nodes.name: Overlap of tau with the ideal correlated state theta
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\theta} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}{\norm{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}}$. Then $$\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^2}{1 + \sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}} \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^3 .$$
assumptions: Let $\ket{\theta} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}{\norm{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}}$.
nodes.label: overlaptau

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5.4
nodes.statement: Consider, \begin{align*} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} &\geq \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{1 - \bra{S} (I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}} & \mbox{(Claim~\ref{claim:tau})}\\ & = \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{2/N-\bra{S}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}} & \mbox{(using $\bra{S}P_A\otimes I_B\ket{S}=\bra{S}I_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}=1/N$)}. \end{align*} By direct calculation, we get $$(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i,j}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\braket{b_j}{a_i}\ket{b_j}\sum_{m=1}^{K\min(a_i,b_j)}\ket{m,m} ;$$ $$\ket{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_i\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\ket{a_i}\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m,m} .$$ Hence, \begin{equation} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2\right)^2}{2-\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2} . \end{equation} Define $R_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } a_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$ and $R'_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } b_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$. Note that both $\{R_{ij}\}$ and $\{R'_{ij}\}$ form probability distributions over $[N^2]$. Also note that $\mathrm{F}(R,R') = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})$. Consider (using relation between fidelity and $\ell_1$ distance, Facts~\ref{fact:fidelityvstrace} and~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi}), \begin{align} \sum_{i,j}\min(R_{ij},R'_{i,j}) & = 1 - \frac{1}{2}\onenorm{R-R'} \geq 1 - \sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(R,R')^2} \nonumber \\ &= 1 - \sqrt{1-(\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})^2} \geq 1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2} . \end{align} Combining Equations~\eqref{eq:thetatau} and~\eqref{eq:minR} we get the desired.
nodes.statement_short: Use Claim 5.3, compute the projected states explicitly, and bound the classical overlap via fidelity and trace distance.

nodes.name: Combine the claims and concavity of fidelity to get fidelity 1-5eps
nodes.statement: From claims \ref{claim:successprob},\ref{claim:relativeprob} and \ref{claim:highprobindex}, the probability that Bob learns the index $j$ is atleast $1-4{\varepsilon}$. Conditioned on this event, Claim \ref{claim:boboutput}, implies that the state $\rho' \in \mathcal{D}(B^j)$ that Bob outputs satisfies $\mathrm{F}(\rho',\rho)\geq 1-{\varepsilon}$. Conditioned on the event that Bob learns the wrong index or the protocol is aborted, let the state output by Bob be $\mu$. Then Bob outputs the state $\tilde{\rho}=\alpha\rho'+(1-\alpha)\mu$, where $\alpha\geq 1-4{\varepsilon}$. Using concavity of fidelity (Fact \ref{fact:fidconcave}), we have $\mathrm{F}(\tilde{\rho},\rho)\geq \alpha\mathrm{F}(\rho',\rho)+(1-\alpha)\mathrm{F}(\mu,\rho) \geq (1-4{\varepsilon})(1-{\varepsilon})\geq 1- 5{\varepsilon}$.

nodes.name: Introduce the k-fold protocol Q and input registers
nodes.statement: Let $\CMcal{Q}$ be a quantum one-way protocol with communication $c\cdot k$ computing $f^k$  with  overall probability of success at least $1-{\varepsilon}$ under distribution $\mu^k$. Let the inputs to Alice and Bob be given in registers $X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. For brevity, we define $X\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. Thus, the state $\sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}$ represents the joint input, where $x$ is drawn from $X$ and $y$ is drawn from $Y$.

nodes.name: Model the protocol's unitaries and the global state
nodes.statement:
Let $\sigma_{E_A,E_B}$ be the shared entanglement between Alice and Bob where register $E_A$ is with Alice and $E_B$ with Bob. Alice applies unitary $U:\CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$, where $E_A\equiv AM$, sends the message register $M$ to Bob, and then Bob applies the unitary $V: \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$, where $ME_B\equiv B'Z$. Since unitary operations by Alice and Bob are conditioned on their respective inputs, the unitaries $U,V$ are  of the form $U=\sum_x\ketbra{x}_X\otimes U_x$ and $V=\sum_y\ketbra{y}_Y\otimes V_y$, where $U_x:\CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$ and $V_y: \CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$.
Let the following be the global state before Alice applies her unitary:
$$\theta_{XYE_AE_B} = \sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}\otimes\sigma_{E_AE_B}.$$

Define random variables $U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$ such that $U_i=X_i$ if $D_i=0$ and $U_i=Y_i$ if $D_i=1$. Let $U=U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$. nodes.name: Conditional independence (Markov chain) of the inputs
nodes.statement:
Let $\rho_{XYAME_BDU}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } U\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU} U^{\dagger}$ be the state after Alice applies her unitary and sends $M$ to Bob. Since $$\condmutinf{XE_AE_B}{Y}{DU}_{\theta}=0,$$ it holds that  
\[\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y}{DU}_{\rho}=0.\]
From the definition of $DU$, we thus have (below $-i$ represents the set $\{1,2\ldots i-1,i+1\ldots k\}$),
\begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_{-i}AE_BM}{Y}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y_{-i}}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=0.
\end{equation}

Consider
\begin{eqnarray*}
2ck&\geq& \mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}\geq \condmutinf{XY}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho}\\ &\geq&\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho} \quad (\text{Fact} ~\ref{fact:chainrulemutualinf})\\
&=& \sum_{i=1}^k \condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{D_iU_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho} 	\\ &=&\frac{1}{2}\br{\sum_{i=1}^k\br{\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{Y_i}{ME_B}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}}}\\
&\geq&\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}.
\end{eqnarray*}
where the last equality is from the definition of $DU$ and the last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}.

nodes.statement_short: Split information over coordinates by the chain rule

nodes.name: Pick a coordinate j with small information; public coins independent of it
nodes.statement:
Hence there exists $j\in[k]$ such that
\begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_j}{ME_B}{Y_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}\leq 4c.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, we have 
\begin{equation} \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}= \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\theta} = 0.
\end{equation}
since the unitary by Alice does not change the state on registers $DUXY$.

nodes.name: Define conditional states of Bob's register
nodes.statement:
For brevity, set $B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } ME_B$. Define the following states, which are obtained by conditioning on various classical registers: $$\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}},$$

$$\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$

$$\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BYDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{YDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$

nodes.statement_short: Define conditional states of Bob's register

nodes.name: Alice's conditional state does not depend on y_j
nodes.statement:
From~(\ref{eqn:dumarkov}), we have
\[\condmutinf{Y}{B}{X_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}=0.\]
which is equivalent to, using Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut} and the fact that registers $X,Y,U,D$ are classical in $\rho_B$: 
$$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}=0.$$ This implies $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ for all $x_j,y_j,d_{-j}u_{-j}$.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Alice's conditional state does not depend on y_j

nodes.name: Average relative entropy at most 4c
nodes.statement:
From~(\ref{eqn:directsummessagelength}), and Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut},
$$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}\leq 4c.$$
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Average relative entropy at most 4c

nodes.name: Markov's inequality on the good set G
nodes.statement:
Let 
$$G\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\set{(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j}):\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}\leq \frac{4c}{\delta}}.$$ By Markov's inequality, 
$$\prob{X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}\in G}\geq1-\delta. $$

nodes.statement_short: Markov's inequality on the good set G

nodes.name: Error analysis of Q'
nodes.statement: From the protocol, it is clear that overall distributional error in $\CMcal{Q}'$ is at most $2\delta+{\varepsilon}$. The error $2\delta$ occurs since the state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfies $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ and the probability that $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\notin G$ is at most $\delta$. The error ${\varepsilon}$ is due to the original protocol $\CMcal{Q}$.

nodes.name: Conclude the direct sum bound
nodes.statement:
Hence 
\[\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+2\delta}{f}\leq \CMcal{O}((c+1)/\delta^9),\]
which implies (changing $\delta\rightarrow \frac{\delta}{2}$)
\[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]

nodes.statement_short: Conclude the direct sum bound

nodes.statement: Let eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$ and of $\sigma$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. Let $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{N}}$ be an orthonormal basis for $\CMcal{H}$. We assume that $a_1, \ldots, a_N, b_1,  \ldots b_N$ are rational numbers and let $K$ be the least common multiple of their denominators. The error due to this assumption goes to $0$ as $K \rightarrow \infty$.

nodes.name: Combine via monotonicity of fidelity
nodes.statement:
Finally  using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}) and Claim~\ref{overlaptau} we get the second part of the theorem as follows. 
\[\sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (E\tau)} \geq  \mathrm{F}(\tau , \ketbra{\theta}) = \sqrt{\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta}} \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^{3/2} . \tag*{\qedhere} \]
nodes.statement_short: Combine via monotonicity of fidelity

nodes.name: State and probability of the event that both succeed at the same index
nodes.statement:
Consider the event that Alice and Bob succeed at the same index. The resulting state in $AA_1BB_1$ is 
$$\frac{(P_A\otimes P_B ) \ket{S}\bra{S} (P_A\otimes P_B)}{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}},$$ 
and this event occurs with probability 
$$\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}^{i} \cdot \bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}= \frac{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}}{1 - \bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: State and probability of the event that both succeed at the same index

nodes.name: Other orders contribute positive operators
nodes.statement: Since the cases of Bob succeeding before Alice and Alice succeeding before Bob add positive operators to $\tau$, we get the desired.

nodes.name: Compute the projected states explicitly
nodes.statement:
By direct calculation, we get 
$$(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i,j}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\braket{b_j}{a_i}\ket{b_j}\sum_{m=1}^{K\min(a_i,b_j)}\ket{m,m} ;$$ 
$$\ket{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_i\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\ket{a_i}\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m,m} .$$ 
Hence,
\begin{equation} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2\right)^2}{2-\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2} .
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Share entangled registers and random hash functions
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Shared resources:} Alice and Bob hold $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$ registers $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ ($i \in [\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil]$), such that $A_1^i\equiv A_1, A^i_2\equiv A_2, B_1^i\equiv B_1,B_2^i\equiv B_2$. The shared state in register $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ is $\ket{S}_{A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i}$. Let $i$ refer to the `index' of corresponding registers.

They also share infinitely many random hash functions $h_1,h_2,\cdots$, where each $h_l:\set{0,\cdots,N-1}\rightarrow\set{0,1}$.

nodes.name: Alice measures with P_A and declares success
nodes.statement:
Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I_A- P_A}$ on each register $A_1^iA^i_2$ where,
\begin{equation} P_A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) .
\end{equation}

On each index $i$, she declares \textit{success} if her outcome corresponds to $P_A$.
nodes.statement_short: Alice measures with P_A and declares success

nodes.name: Bob measures with P_B and declares success
nodes.statement:
Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I_B- P_B}$ on each register $B_1^iB^i_2$ where,
\begin{equation} P_B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'} b_i,K\}}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) .
\end{equation}

On each index $i$, he declares \textit{success} if his outcome corresponds to $P_B$.
nodes.statement_short: Bob measures with P_B and declares success

nodes.name: Abort if Alice never succeeds
nodes.statement: If Alice does not succeed on any index, she aborts.
nodes.statement_short: Abort if Alice never succeeds

nodes.name: Alice sends the block of her first success
nodes.statement: Else, Alice selects the first index $m$ where she succeeds and sends to Bob the binary encoding of $k=\lceil m/N\rceil$ using $\lceil\log\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil$ bits.
nodes.statement_short: Alice sends the block of her first success

nodes.name: Alice sends hash values of her index
nodes.statement: Alice sends $\{ h_l(m\mod N) |~ l \in  [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]\}$  to Bob.
nodes.statement_short: Alice sends hash values of her index

nodes.name: Bob picks the first accepted index matching the hashes and outputs it
nodes.statement: Define $S_B \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \{ t |~ \text{ Bob succeeds on index } $t$\} \cap \{(k-1)N,  \cdots, k N -1\}$. If $S_B$ is empty, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$. Bob selects the first index $n$ in $S_B$ such that $\forall l \in  [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]: h_l(n \mod N) = h_l(m \mod N) $ and outputs the state in $B_1^n$ (if no such index exists, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$).
nodes.statement_short: Bob picks the first accepted index matching the hashes and outputs it

nodes.name: Share public coins and entanglement for protocol P
nodes.statement: Alice and Bob share public coins according to distribution $\rho_{D_{-j}U_{-j}}$, and the shared entanglement needed to run the protocol $\CMcal{P}$ from Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol}.

nodes.name: Embed the input in coordinate j
nodes.statement: Alice and Bob are given the input  $(x,y)\sim\mu$. They embed the input to the $j$-th coordinate $X_jY_j$. The input is independent of shared randomness, from equation (\ref{eqn:directsumpubliccoins}).

nodes.name: Identify the states known to each party
nodes.statement: Given input $(x_j,y_j)\equiv (x,y)$ and shared public coins $d_{-j}u_{-j}$, Alice knows the eigen-decomposition of the state $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, since $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$. Bob knows the eigen-decomposition of state $\rho_{B}^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$.

nodes.statement_short: Identify the states known to each party

nodes.name: Run protocol P of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: They  run the protocol in Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol} with inputs $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Alice) and $\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Bob). After communicating $\mathcal{O}(4c/\delta^9)$  bits to Bob, Bob receives a state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfying $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ if $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\in G$.

nodes.statement_short: Run protocol P of Theorem 3.1

nodes.name: Bob samples the remaining inputs
nodes.statement: Bob samples the distribution from $\rho_{Y_{-j}}$, since he has the registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. This is possible from equation \ref{eqn:dumarkov}, which states that register $Y_{-j}$ is independent of registers $A,B,X$ conditioned on registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$.
